headline: At least five drivers carry grid penalties in Las Vegas
body: Sainz and Stroll lose 10 places and Antonelli five. Bearman is set to start at the back after taking a substantial number of new engine parts. Piastri's 10-place penalty makes five.

headline: No lap times set in Las Vegas FP1
body: Seventeen drivers went out on full wets in heavy rain and standing water, and none tried a flying lap. Haas could not use the new rear wing it brought.

headline: Russell tops damp Las Vegas FP2 as Verstappen reports no power
body: Russell went fastest on a 1m47.272s, 0.071s ahead of Gasly, with Leclerc third and Hadjar fourth. Verstappen did nine laps, the fewest of anyone, and said the car had the same problems he reported in Brazil practice.

headline: F1 agrees in principle to bring back V8 engines in 2030
body: McLaren's Zak Brown confirmed an agreement in principle on a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 with less hybrid assistance. The signatures are not yet on paper, and the regulations are due before the FIA World Motor Sport Council in Shanghai next month.

headline: Cadillac delays its own power unit to 2030
body: Cadillac will stay a Ferrari customer through 2029 and bring its own power unit online in 2030 with the V8, a year later than planned. CEO Dan Towriss said its Charlotte power unit facility opens on 18 December.
